text:
The boardroom in Brisco County was quiet on the afternoon of March 14, 2024, the quiet that falls when a routine agenda item turns out not to be routine. At the board's regular public session, Dolores Venkataraman, the county auditor, rose to present the Brisco County Fiscal Year 2022-23 Performance Audit.

Her conclusion was plain. The audit found that $2.3 million in road maintenance funds could not be accounted for.

Roads are public business that residents notice mostly when it fails: the pothole that returns each spring, the shoulder that crumbles after rain. Maintenance money exists to prevent that, quietly. That $2.3 million cannot be traced raises a question larger than any ledger: how a community knows its money went where it was promised.
